 b. Outgoing Mayor’s Comments
  Mayor Devine stated it has been another difficult year on many levels: COVID-19 and issues
  of residences and businesses have had to endure. With collaboration with staff and Council,
  they have worked hard to make the rebound from the pandemic easier and smoother. She
  thanked her colleagues for trusting her to lead. Things that were done: collaborative effort
  during the pandemic with different departments and agencies – hosting vaccine clinics,
  providing supplies such as masks and sanitizers, homework assistance during lockdown,
  delivery of food services, ensuring safety and well-being of residents. Accomplishments of
  Council: approval of three affordable housing project, approving the Sundown Town
  Resolution, establishing outdoor dining in Montrose, banning the sale of flavored tobacco and
  vaping products, banning the sale of Mylar balloon, banning the use of single-use plastic,
  approval of the Scholl Biogas project, signing to support the Net Zero Carbon Footprints, and
  approval of clean energy programs. Council has encouraged staff to convert to electric power
  equipment such as leaf blowers for our parks. Eight parks have now been designated as
  certified “green zones.” She announced that Glendale is the first city to conduct research and
  development on automated electric mower equipment. GWP is on track to install 27 new
  charging stations by next month. The future of transportation is bright for the city: bus rapid
  transit to provide connectivity between Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, street car
  trolley in the Downtown Glendale area, designated bike lanes, and brightly colored
  crosswalks. The city is working on having Wi-Fi in parks. Council approved the Blue Ribbon
  Panel Pension Reform, Landlord/Tenant Committee, and Sustainability Committee. The
  Stone Barn Nature Center was recently completed. Council also gathered for the
  groundbreaking of the Armenian-American Museum and looked forward to the Central Park
  that will surround that area. The design for the Artsakh paseo has also been approved. The
  Verdugo Wash Project is also in the early stages of planning providing connectivity for
  pedestrians and cyclists from North to South Glendale. Art installation around the city is also
  being planned. Even though most of the year the city was either in lockdown or zoom calls,
  Council and staff worked together to accomplish many things. Council approved the increase
  of supply of affordable housing, passed ordinances that would protect the neighborhoods and
  the residents’ quality of life. Council supported environmental projects, working on a pathway
  to 100% renewable energy. They worked on street-safety for pedestrians and cyclists,
  cultural and entertainment objectives, and encouragement of the art throughout the city.
  Council developed connectivity improvements through transportation, walkways, and
  pathways, and trails. A significant movement was made in the direction of electrification of
  the city. As a last act of being Mayor, Council approved and attended the unveiling of the
  Filipino-American Friendship Monument, a first in California. She thanked staff and
  colleagues for working so hard and thanked the residents as well and it has been an honor
  and a privilege for her to serve.

  Public Comments:
  David Eisenberg
  Senator Anthony Portantino

d. New Mayor’s Comments
  Newly Appointed Mayor Ardy Kassakhian thanked former Mayor Paula Devine, for her above
  and beyond service, even during facing a personal loss. The city has witnessed Council
  Members and former Mayors Agajanian and Devine’s leadership during unprecedented times
  as they led us through this pandemic. He also thanked former and elected officials that are in
  attendance or watching the meeting. He spoke about the struggles we faced during the
  pandemic and the wars that happened globally. The city hall welcomes everyone back with
  enthusiasm and commitment to excellent service which has always been the hallmark of the
  city and staff. Council will not seek any measures to make inconvenience or injury on anyone
  and only on the best interest for the city and pray that the worst is behind us. It is not an easy
  task but what Council does, and in collaboration with other agencies, is to make the citizens’
  lives as safe, as prosperous, and as happy as possible. Council’s job is to make the city the
  best that it can be, that we all must strive towards a more perfect union that shall not perish
  from this earth. He is committed to doing this job to the best of his abilities. Because Council
  all want what is best for Glendale, it does not mean they will all agree on how to get there.
  Sometimes there are disagreements on the dais and the public. There is clash among the
  residents, landlords, tenants, homeowners, business owners, etc. but that chaos and the back
  and forth is democracy. As much as we hate “noise,” that argument is what sits at the heart of
  our system. This is how we make things better and it can be annoying but in that you get a
  voice. If the city wants a better Glendale, we cannot run away from the argument but must run
  towards it and participate. As Mayor, he will have definite opinions on issues of the day and
  vote on how his conscience and constituents dictate. Although he will not win on every fight
  nor have secrets to have everyone get along and come to an agreement, what he brings to
  this job is his willingness to try, fight on, and push forward. In this job, a person needs to have
  an open ear, and an even more open heart. He promises to come to this dais every week with
  both and only ask to do the same from the public. He will outline his plan for the next year in
  the upcoming weeks. He will also continue to listen to the public by holding regular office
  hours as he does every Friday in Montrose and hoped to extend them to other parts of the city
  soon. He will also ask staff to bring back the “City Council in Your Neighborhood Program” to
  ensure that we are hearing from every part of the city in the residents’ terms and
  neighborhoods about their issues. As the city emerges from the pandemic, Council will focus
  on recovery and growth and supporting the local businesses and ensuring that the process of
  doing business in Glendale is smooth, simple, and efficient. He wants to assure the public that
  the city has one of the best people working for this organization. Staff has worked tirelessly
  through staffing cutbacks, budget reduction, and a pandemic. He thanked staff for making
  Council look good. He pledges to continue the city’s pursuit of sustainable and conservation
  focus policy. The city has done so much already from placing restrictions on Mylar balloons
  and single-use plastics, to rethinking energy priorities and how Council meet the growing
  needs of the city. Mr. Kassakhian will continue to be a strong advocate for the libraries and
  arts and culture in the city. The city faced a lot of hard truth about racism, discrimination,
  04 05 22
  CC
   gender and equality and we’ll continue to work on these issues but by learning, we will make
  progress. Sometimes there is setback but the goal is always moving forward including
  acknowledging and admitting when we have been wrong. America is at its best when we
  celebrate our uniqueness and the people of all races and ethnicities who have contributed to
  this country’s success. He will continue to be an advocate for all under-represented voices to
  have a voice and to have an opportunity to serve on our city boards, commissions,
  committees, and wherever we need to have our residents’ voices heard. Additionally, he will
  ask staff to organize the city’s first book fair and will ask Council to support this initiative. The
  city loves libraries and we have amazing writers, musicians, artists, and authors that call
  Glendale home. This will highlight their work and bring the community closer together. He will
  continue to pursue government reform, promoting transparency and accountability. He will
  also ask staff to begin the process of a Charter Review Committee to be in line with where we
  are today and where we want to be as a city in the future. He will also ask staff to initiate a
  Civic Academy designed for individuals who want to be more engaged in civic life to learn
  about each department, how the city functions, and intricacies of the budget, and finance
  processes. The city has a Citizens Police Academy and the Chamber of Commerce has its
  own leadership program, but the city does not have a program that serves as a training
  ground for our boards and commissions and ultimately future council members. Most
  importantly he promises to pursue every cooperation and collaboration with the school district
  and the community college to improve the city. He had a dream to double the amount of open
  and usable parks spaces in the densest parts of the city and must and should open school
  yards for neighborhood access and he will not rest until we do. Children’s mental health is at
  stake coming out of this pandemic and should not delay these efforts. He will ask staff and
  Council to help push forward to work with the schools to make this happen. There is more that
  he wants to do but doing just these things and carrying out other responsibilities and important
  issues in the horizon will take up a lot of time. Council is inundating staff so much to a level
  that the city ends up municipal paralysis or even low morale. He thanked Dveen Babaian and
  Sevana Zadorian for being the backbones of his campaign. He thanked his wife, Courtney and
  son, Armen, the reason why he gets up every morning and put his heart and everything into
  this work. He thanked his family members for their support and sometimes believes in him
  more than he believes in himself. He thanked his parents who have taught him the most
  important thing in the world, the importance of service, sacrifice, unconditional love, and to
  always be proud of his culture and heritage. In closing, he thanked Glendale, colleagues, for
  entrusting him this tremendous responsibility. Their work is cut-out for them but will rise to the
  challenge.
